key_insight: Elastic turbulence simulations can remain physically useful even when local conformation-tensor positive-definiteness is violated, as long as the run stays above a minimum resolution and below the unstable regime.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce the computational cost of direct numerical simulations of polymeric flows by relaxing the need for extremely high resolutions that strictly preserve positive-definiteness.
method: Simulate dilute polymer flow in a low-Re plane channel using a conformation-tensor model.
Sweep numerical resolution to identify instability and positivity-preserving thresholds.
Compare mid-plane velocity, gradient, and polymer-stretch statistics against fully positive-definite reference runs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two resolution thresholds: below one the solver blows up, above another it stays positive-definite, and in between the simulations remain stable and chaotic while matching key mid-plane statistics from fully positive-definite simulations.
watch_item: The result appears to hold for the reported channel-flow elastic-turbulence setup, so applicability to other geometries, parameter regimes, or long-time observables may require separate validation.
paper_title: No need to stay positive: a practical approach to direct numerical simulations of elastic turbulence
